name: Light Khaki
lede: Light Khaki is a pale, yellow-green khaki, built from the modifier "light" rather than drawn from any dated military or dye source.

sections.title: A tint of khaki
sections.body:
The 2010 xkcd color survey is the only source we hold for this exact word pairing [1]. Our library's plain [[khaki|Khaki]] entry traces to 1848 through Maerz and Paul, when the word still meant dust-colored cloth before it meant any particular hex, but Light Khaki itself carries no such date: it is simply that older color, lightened [2].

ISCC-NBS 1955 would file this pale tint as a light yellow green, and the nearest library neighbors are [[cream|Cream]] and [[key-lime|Key Lime]] [3]. It reads as [[khaki|khaki]] drained toward a pastel, with most of the brown pulled out and the green pushed forward [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, carries this color in 6 paintings at five percent coverage or more, the earliest a 1642 [[painting:rijks-200108812|Still Life]] by Gerret Willemsz Heda [4]. The strongest single match is a 19th-century painting, *The Cat*, covering about 28 percent of the canvas [4]. These are museum photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so a match is a screen color, not a pigment identification [4].
